title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendor, travel, and templates
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary
This document consolidates the company-wide policies and core operational processes used by Redwood Inference for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, hiring managers, and approvers.

Scope and purpose
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors that interact with Redwood systems and data.
- Purpose: Provide consistent, auditable processes that balance velocity with risk controls and compliance needs.

1) Access & permissions (RBAC and onboarding/offboarding)
Overview
Redwood uses role-based access control (RBAC) as the default permission model for internal systems (IAM, Okta, internal console). Principle of least privilege (POLP) must be applied.
Key policies
- Access request: All access requests must be submitted via the Access Request form (link in templates). Requests must list business justification, duration (if temporary), and approver.
- Approvals: Manager approval required for non-admin access. Security or Platform approval required for admin, production, or cross-team access.
- Time-bound access: Temporary access limited to a maximum of 90 days unless extension is approved by owner_team.
- Periodic reviews: Quarterly access reviews led by team owners. Outstanding access older than 60 days without justification will be flagged for removal.
- Service accounts: Must be identifiable, have owner team, and rotate credentials per secrets policy.

Onboarding and offboarding checklist (high level)
1. New hire onboarding: create Okta account, assign standard team role, + provision additional product-specific roles via access request.
2. Contractor: time-boxed access, sponsor + security review for elevated access.
3. Offboarding: immediate removal of Okta account, revoke third-party tokens, rotate affected service credentials, escalate if access to production systems was used.

Owner and SLAs
- Owner: People Ops (owner_team) + Security (for production access).
- SLA: Standard provisioning completed within 48 business hours for approved requests; emergency access handled by Security with 4-hour SLA during business hours.

2) Change management
Objective
Ensure safe, observable, and reversible changes across infra, runtime, and customer-facing services while minimizing unplanned outages.
Classification
- Standard change: Low-risk, pre-authorized (e.g., routine config updates).
- Planned change: Requires change advisory board (CAB) sign-off if impacting production SLOs.
- Emergency change: Fast-tracked; must be documented and reviewed post-incident.

Process (planned changes)
1. Submit change ticket to Change Board system with: scope, rollback plan, validation checklist, owner, and maintenance window.
2. Runbook & testing: Include pre-change test results and canary validation plan.
3. CAB review: CAB meets twice daily for high-throughput windows; only changes with clear rollback are approved.
4. Execute in maintenance window with traceability (tracing hooks enabled).
5. Post-change verification and monitoring (48-hour watch).

Emergency change procedure
1. Mark ticket as EMERGENCY and notify oncall@redwood.com and the SRE leader.
2. Apply minimal fix, capture live diagnostics, and apply short-lived mitigation if needed.
3. Postmortem: Full postmortem must be filed within 5 business days.

Change guardrails and thresholds
- No single change should increase error budget consumption by >10% without escalation.
- Rollback plan required for any change that touches production data paths.

Owner and review cadence
- Owner: Eng SRE.
- CAB: cross-functional representation from Eng Platform, Eng Infra, Security, Product.

3) Data management (classification, retention, encryption)
Data classification levels
- Public: Allowed for external sharing.
- Internal: General internal business information.
- Confidential: Customer data, PII, keys, or anything that could cause harm if disclosed.
- Restricted: Highly sensitive regulated data (HIPAA, PCI, etc.).

Storage and encryption
- All Confidential & Restricted data must be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed) and in transit (TLS v1.2+).
- Backups: Encrypted backups retained per retention schedule.

Retention & deletion policy (summary table)
| Data type | Retention period | Responsible team |
| Customer logs (Confidential) | 1 year (default) | Eng SRE |
| Audit logs (Internal) | 3 years | Security |
| Financial records | 7 years | Finance |

Data access and handling
- Data minimization: Only store data necessary for product function.
- Masking: PII must be masked or redacted in non-production environments.
- Data exports: Exports require Data Owner approval and must be tracked.

Owner & compliance
- Owner: Security & Data Privacy.
- Annual review: Data retention and classification reviewed yearly or when regulations change.

4) Procurement & expenses
Overview
Procurement and incidental expenses are governed to control spend, ensure vendor compliance, and maintain accurate financial records.
Thresholds and approvals
- $0–$2,500: Manager approval.
- $2,501–$25,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- >$25,000: VP-level approval + procurement lead + legal review.
- One-time quick purchases under $250 may be reimbursed via expense claim with manager receipt.

Vendor & contract process (procurement steps)
1. Need identification and business justification.
2. Procurement request submitted in procurement system with ROI and budget code.
3. Vendor selection: at least one commercial quote; three quotes preferred for >$25k.
4. Legal & Security review for contracts with data access.
5. PO issuance and invoice routing to AP.

Expenses & travel reimbursements
- Use company card where available; out-of-pocket expenses require receipts.
- Expense submission deadline: within 30 days of transaction. Late submissions may be rejected.
- Per diem and allowed items: see Travel section below for thresholds.

Owner and records
- Owner: Finance & Procurement.
- Records retention: Contracts and POs stored for 7 years.

5) Vendor management and security assessment
Vendor classification
- Tier A (High risk): Vendors with access to production systems, customer data, or who process payments. Requires full security questionnaire and SOC2/ISO evidence.
- Tier B (Medium risk): Vendors that integrate with internal tools but do not store customer data. Require a questionnaire and targeted controls.
- Tier C (Low risk): SaaS with no integration to internal systems; basic vendor registration.

Onboarding checklist
1. Business case & budget approval.
2. Security questionnaire and risk assessment by Security team.
3. Contract with appropriate SLAs, data processing addendum (DPA) if needed.
4. Vendor onboarding in asset inventory with owner and renewal date.

Offboarding and contract end
- Notify vendor 90 days ahead of contract end for renewal planning.
- Revoke any credentials, remove API keys, and rotate affected secrets.
- Archive contract & evidence of data deletion where applicable.

Owner and renewal cadence
- Owner: Finance & Security.
- Renewal review at T-90 days (automated calendar reminder).

6) Travel policy (business travel and approvals)
Booking and approvals
- Domestic travel: Manager approval for trips >$500 or >2 days.
- International travel: Requires manager + People Ops approval and a security/travel risk review for certain countries.
- Class of travel: Economy for flights <6 hours; Premium Economy or Business requires VP approval.

Allowed expenses and per diems
- Meals: per diem based on destination (template). Alcohol covered when part of official meal with client and within per-diem.
- Hotels: Preferred vendor rates or mid-range business hotels.
- Ground transport: Use rideshare or public transit; car rental with insurance pre-approved.

Pre-trip security & insurance
- International travelers must register trip with People Ops and provide emergency contact.
- Company travel insurance covers medical evacuation for approved trips when required.

Owner and compliance
- Owner: People Ops & Finance.
- Expense audit: Finance performs quarterly travel expense audit for policy compliance.

7) Internal templates & links (quick start)
Included templates (location: /confluence/templates)
- Access request form (access-request-template.md)
- Procurement request template (procurement-request-template.md)
- Vendor risk assessment checklist (vendor-risk-checklist.md)
- Change request template (change-request-template.md)
- Travel request form (travel-request-template.md)
- Postmortem template (postmortem-template.md)

How to use templates
1. Copy the template into your team space and fill required fields.
2. Attach supporting artifacts (screenshots, logs, vendor quotes).
3. Route for approval via the designated workflow in the template.

Governance, exceptions, and escalation
- Exceptions: Requests for permanent exceptions to policy must be submitted to Risk & Exceptions with a business justification and mitigation plan. Exceptions older than 12 months must be re-evaluated.
- Escalation path: Manager -> Director -> VP -> Risk & Compliance Committee.

Audit and reporting
- Quarterly compliance reports from People Ops, Finance, and Security.
- Internal audits: annual reviews of access controls, procurement spend, and vendor inventory.

Document maintenance and feedback
- This document owner (People Ops) is responsible for annual review or sooner when regulatory or business changes occur.
- To propose changes, submit a request using the policy change template and tag the reviewers.

Appendix: Quick reference tables
- Procurement approvals: see "Thresholds and approvals" above.
- Data classification decisions: refer to Data Classification Decision Log (linked in related_pages).
